# dsh-shooter
A top-down arena shooter that opens as a full panel in DeepSeek Harness, reached from a crosshair en
try in the left sidebar.
中文说明
## What it does
The sidebar entry opens a self-contained arena shooter rendered on a canvas: survive ever-larger wav
es of enemies, keep your health bar above zero, and restart when the run ends. The panel chrome (hea
der, buttons, overlays) is drawn with the harness theme tokens, so it follows the active light or da
rk theme; the playfield keeps its own dark palette.
- **Waves.** Each wave queues more enemies than the last; a new wave starts once the field is clear.
Every fifth wave adds a boss: a big armoured elite that charges and fires radial bursts, with its o
wn health bar across the top of the field and a guaranteed pair of health drops when it dies. Runs a
lso throw in **charge waves** (a line of runners pushing in from one side) and gunners that keep swi

tching flanks, so the arena does not settle into a shooting gallery.
- **Combo multiplier.** Kills c
hained within three seconds are worth more: the third quick kill doubles the score, the sixth triple
s it. The multiplier shows as ×2 / ×3 beside the score and drops back to ×1 after three seconds with

out a kill.
- **In-run upgrades.** Clearing every second wave offers a pick of three upgrades — dama
ge, fire rate, twin shots, piercing rounds, move speed, dash cooldown, longer combo window, pickup m
agnet, a regenerating shield, or extra max health. Click a card or press `1` / `2` / `3`; the run fr

eezes until one is chosen. Picks are stacked and shown as small badges in the bottom-left corner.
-
**Watch controls.** A speed chip cycles playback between 0.25×, 0.5×, 1× and 2×, and a skill chip cy
cles the autopilot through rookie / normal / master (reaction time, aim lead, dodge weight). Both li
ve in the bottom-right corner during a run and next to the start buttons on the idle screen, and bot

h are remembered across reloads. Turning calm mode on drops a still-1× run to 0.5× automatically.
-
**Four enemy types.** Grunts chase you, runners are fast and fragile, tanks are slow and armoured, g

unners keep their distance and shoot back.
- **Dash.** A short burst with a few invulnerable frames

— the way out of a corner.
- **Health pickups.** A small chance to drop from a defeated enemy.

## Controls
| Input | Action |

| `W` `A` `S` `D` | Move |
| Mouse | Aim |
| Hold left button | Fire |
| `Shift` | Dash |
| `1` `2`

`3` | Pick an upgrade card |
| `Esc` | Pause / resume (or leave big screen) |
Keys only steer the game while its panel is the visible one, so typing in the chat composer never mo
the game while its panel is the visible one, so typing in the chat composer never moves the player.
## Watch mode (大肥鱼 autopilot)
The idle screen offers two ways in: **Let Da Feiyu play (watch)** starts a run with the AI pilot in
control, while **Play myself** starts a normal run. In watch mode the player sprite becomes Da Feiyu
— a round blue fish with a gun — wearing a name tag and a live state label (hunting / kiting / dodg
ing / dashing / healing / cruising). The header keeps a pilot switch so you can hand the controls ba
ck at any time, and when the fish goes down it redeems itself automatically after a couple of second
s instead of making you click retry.
The pilot reads the same game state a human does (enemies, incoming bullets, pickups, walls), then w
rites a movement vector and a fire/dash decision into the normal input channel, so both modes share
the same physics. It dodges bullets by sliding perpendicular to the shot line, keeps range against m
elee enemies while orbiting gunners, backs off to heal below 78 HP, and leads its shots by the bulle
t travel time. Player keyboard and pointer input are ignored while the pilot is on.
## Pet commentary (optional)
Watch mode also narrates itself. One-way and best-effort, it POSTs lines to the local **dsh-pet** pl
ugin's third-party feed endpoint (`/dsh-pet-7340/broadcast?pet=main&surface=any`) and the desktop pe
t says them in its speech bubble. Every event has several phrasings (`game.report.*` in `client.js`)
, which are picked at random and never repeat back-to-back, so the commentary stops sounding like a
loop: first blood, five-kill streaks (at most once per 20 seconds), one low-health callout per run,
health packs, boss arrivals and boss kills, every other wave, every 1000 points, a new personal reco
rd, and every death — plus a "back again" line when the autopilot restarts. Regular lines are thrott
led to one every ~7 seconds; a death always plays. The game never waits on the pet: if dsh-pet is mi
ssing, asleep, muted, or owned by another plugin, the messages are simply skipped.
The pet id is the `pet=main` part of `PET_BROADCAST_URL` in `client.js` — change it if your pet is c
onfigured under another id. The spoken lines live in the `game.report.*` dictionary keys and are eas
er another id. The spoken lines live in the `game.report.*` dictionary keys and are easy to rewrite.
Each line is also **voiced**: the same text is sent to the pet's TTS endpoint (`/dsh-pet-7340/voice/
speak`) and the returned MP3 is played in the page, so you hear the commentary without flipping the
pet's own speech master switch in its settings. Synthesis failures (offline, no provider) only cost
the sound — the bubble still appears. Since the bubble is posted with `surface=any` (no `voiceTo`),
enabling the pet's own speech later does not double-play these lines.
## Quality of life
- **Fixed timestep.** The simulation always advances in 1/60 s steps, so a 144 Hz display no longer
makes the game run at double speed; frames that arrive late are caught up in at most five steps, and

a tab returning from the background does not fast-forward.
- **Persistent best score.** The best sc
ore is saved to `localStorage` (`dsh-shooter:best`) and shown on the idle screen and the game-over s

creen.
- **Big screen.** The header's **Big screen** button promotes the panel to a full-viewport ov
erlay so you can watch from across the room; `Esc` or the same button takes you back. The canvas res

izes with it.
